summary: Public analysis resets compiler-global load-path state without restoring the caller's configuration
evidence: Arch_guard.render_json/render_text are installed public entry points and call Guard_interpreter.analyze. analyze invokes Load_path.init with only Config.standard_library and Envaux.reset_cache. Compiler-libs documents Load_path.init as reset followed by adding only supplied paths. A compiler-only owned client initialized a fresh marker path, called render_json on the already-built owned arch_index.cmt, and printed before_marker=true after_marker=false (compile exit 0, run exit 0).
fix: Prefer keeping the analyzer process-isolated behind the CLI unless in-process composability is explicitly required. If it is required, define the contract, encapsulate and serialize all compiler-global mutation, and test success/exception restoration. Restoring get_paths plus resetting Envaux caches is incomplete by itself because the auto-include callback and Envaux cache state are separate mutable globals.
boundary: installed arch-index.guard render API to host compiler-libs process
invariant: A public library call must not silently destroy compiler-global lookup configuration owned by its caller.
failure_mode: Subsequent host environment reconstruction or compiler lookup fails or resolves differently because only the standard-library path remains.
